head: 82d3aa49d0e4e00591478f4a78e32f3c771a742c
summary:
Attempt 2 discharges O-001 and O-002 in the code. Both refusals now name the parent that carries the attribute and give `compact /u /s:"<parent>"`. The builder measured that form and declared it; my `/s "folder"` wording was wrong. SmbLibraryPinTests now refuses a csproj that redefines either pin property. On 82d3aa4 the full suite passed 400/400. The nine tests in the four changed classes passed, including WindowCasesIsAscii and the 5.1 and 7 parses. No comment, doc or message elsewhere still describes the old '%TEMP% or a folder above it' / `compact /u` remedy. The rewritten NewCaseFolderRefusesACompressedTempByName has two new input-shape defects, both in its assertions. (1) It checks the made folder's attributes by string prefix, "made Directory ". I measured that new folders inherit NotContentIndexed, so on a TEMP drive with content indexing turned off the default suite fails there, blaming compression. (2) It recovers the refused leaf's path by splitting on the first space. With a space anywhere in %TEMP%, its 'left behind' check tests the wrong path and passes vacuously; the version it replaced asserted this robustly.

Second round: This round's walk found one new defect: SmbLibraryPinTests' XML reading still lets through per-project overrides that MSBuild accepts. The rest of attempt 2 held when I pushed on it. I ran the refusal's printed remedy, `compact /u /s:"<parent>"`, pasted as text into both pwsh 7 and Windows PowerShell 5.1 on a parent whose path contains spaces. Both exited 0 and cleared the parent and its old subfolder. The New-CaseFolder test's line parsing trims CRLF. When the first call does not refuse, $message is $null and the test fails loudly. The TempTree test's regex and cmd.exe quoting hold for paths with spaces and parentheses.

findings.claim: NewCaseFolderRefusesACompressedTempByName decides whether the case folder made after the remedy is uncompressed by string prefix. The pwsh script prints 'made ' + [System.IO.File]::GetAttributes($made), and the test asserts lines[2].StartsWith("made Directory "). Any other attribute the folder inherits breaks that prefix. I measured that NotContentIndexed is inherited: a folder with it set gave 'Directory, NotContentIndexed' on a child and on a grandchild made with CreateDirectory. It is set on everything on a drive whose 'Allow files on this drive to have contents indexed' box is cleared, a common setting. On such a TEMP drive the line reads 'made Directory, NotContentIndexed ...' and this default-suite test fails with 'after the refusal's remedy, the next case folder was refused or came out compressed', blaming compression when the folder is plain. An EFS-encrypted %TEMP% (inherited Encrypted) fails the same way. The sibling tests already check the flag itself: TempTreeTests uses HasFlag(Compressed), and so does NewFileTakesItsSizeOnDiskInACompressedFolder.
findings.evidence: tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/WindowCasesHelperTests.cs, NewCaseFolderRefusesACompressedTempByName: the script's "'made ' + [System.IO.File]::GetAttributes($made) + ' ' + $made" and the assertion `lines[2].StartsWith("made Directory ", StringComparison.Ordinal)`. My run: a parent with NotContentIndexed set gave 'child: Directory, NotContentIndexed' and 'leaf: Directory, NotContentIndexed'.
findings.fix: Print the flag rather than the whole attribute set, e.g. "'made compressed=' + [System.IO.File]::GetAttributes($made).HasFlag([System.IO.FileAttributes]::Compressed)", and assert that lines[2] starts with "made compressed=False".

findings.claim: Attempt 2 replaced the check that the refused case folder is not left behind with `string refusedFolder = lines[0]["refused ".Length..].Split(' ')[0]; Assert.False(Directory.Exists(refusedFolder), ...)`. The refused path is %TEMP%\...\fsa-window-cases\<guid>, and it is followed in the message by ' came out NTFS-compressed ...'. Splitting on the first space cuts the path wherever %TEMP% itself has a space, for example C:\Users\John Smith\AppData\Local\Temp gives 'C:\Users\John'. The assertion then tests a path that is not the case folder and passes whether or not New-CaseFolder removed the leaf. The version it replaced asserted this robustly (fsa-window-cases empty or absent). So a regression in the `[System.IO.Directory]::Delete($folder)` line of the refusal would go unseen on such a machine.
findings.evidence: tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/WindowCasesHelperTests.cs, NewCaseFolderRefusesACompressedTempByName: `lines[0]["refused ".Length..].Split(' ')[0]`; the message comes from tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 New-CaseFolder: "$folder came out NTFS-compressed and was removed: ..."
findings.fix: Cut at the message's own delimiter instead of the first space: `string line = lines[0]; string refusedFolder = line["refused ".Length..line.IndexOf(" came out NTFS-compressed", StringComparison.Ordinal)];`. Alternatively, assert that fsa-window-cases holds exactly one entry, the folder named on the 'made' line.

findings.claim: SmbLibraryPinTests still reads the projects as plain XML, so several MSBuild-legal ways of bumping SMBLibrary in one project pass the guard. (a) An item update in one csproj, `<ItemGroup><PackageReference Update="SMBLibrary" Version="1.6.0" /></ItemGroup>`, changes the evaluated version. The loop selects only elements whose Include equals the package, so this element is never examined, and it defines no property, so the new redefinition assertion misses it too. (b) MSBuild property names are case-insensitive. `<FsaSMBLibraryVersion>1.6.0</FsaSMBLibraryVersion>` in a csproj overrides the pin, but `Descendants(property)` matches the XName exactly, so the redefinition assertion (and the once-only count in Directory.Build.props) misses it. (c) A redefinition or Update in a .props or .targets under tests/ (a nested Directory.Build.props that imports the root one, or an imported file) is never read, because the scan is `*.csproj` only. Each of these gives StallRig and Core.Tests different SMBLibrary versions with the test green: HF-013's failure, found at run time in the network cases. R2-m3 closed only the plain same-case property redefinition.
findings.evidence: tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/SmbLibraryPinTests.cs: the loop `Directory.EnumerateFiles(Path.Combine(repo, "tests"), "*.csproj", ...)`, the redefinition check `XDocument.Load(project).Descendants(property).Any()` (case-sensitive XName), and the reference filter `string.Equals((string?)e.Attribute("Include"), package, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)` (Include only, never Update)
findings.fix: Robust: ask MSBuild instead of reading XML. Run `dotnet msbuild <csproj> -getItem:PackageReference` (SDK 8+) for Core.Tests and StallRig, and assert that the evaluated Version of SMBLibrary and of SMBLibrary.Win32 is the same in both and equal to the Directory.Build.props pin. That catches every override form at once. Smallest, if the XML approach is kept: select PackageReference elements by Include OR Update (split on ';' and trimmed); compare property element names with StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase, both in the csproj loop and in the Directory.Build.props count; and scan *.props and *.targets under tests/ as well as *.csproj.

obligations.evidence: tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 New-CaseFolder: after deleting the leaf, $parent = Split-Path -Parent $folder, and the throw says "$parent is NTFS-compressed ... compact /u /s:`"$parent`"". tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/TempTree.cs CreateRoot: parent = Path.GetDirectoryName(root), with the same wording. TempTreeTests.ATreeRootUnderACompressedFolderIsRefusedByName and WindowCasesHelperTests.NewCaseFolderRefusesACompressedTempByName each run the printed remedy through cmd.exe and then make a folder that is not compressed under a still-compressed temp; both passed in my run. The remedy form differs from my suggested fix, which the builder measured and declared.

tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/SmbLibraryPinTests.cs csproj loop: `Assert.True(!XDocument.Load(project).Descendants(property).Any(), $"{relative} redefines {property}; it is pinned once in Directory.Build.props.")` for both pin properties. It passed on the current tree, and StallRig.csproj is unchanged from 8226df6.
tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 All list (Run section) still omits T-005; this attempt did not touch it.
Directory.Build.props pins both versions once, and both csproj files use $(FsaSmbLibraryVersion) and $(FsaSmbLibraryWin32Version). The guard is now complete per O-002.

The New-CaseFolder and TempTree.CreateRoot refusals and New-File's Random(20) bytes stand, and the refusal message is now correct (O-001). The m4 and m5 defects are in the test's assertions, not in the fix.
tests/window/FsaWindowHook/StartupHook.cs is unchanged since attempt 1, where I ran H-003 and it passed.

drift: Declared, and correct: the refusals print `compact /u /s:"<parent>"` (colon form), not the `compact /u /s "<parent>"` that R2-m2's fix text proposed. The builder measured the proposed form clearing only the folder's own attribute. The parent is left in place rather than deleted when it is empty.

Declared under m1's deferral: attempt 2 adds another hand-rolled process harness, TempTreeTests.Cmd, plus an inline ProcessStartInfo inside the pwsh script of NewCaseFolderRefusesACompressedTempByName. The deferred Core.Tests tidy slice should take these too.

The remedy fixes the folder, not %TEMP%. If Disk Cleanup or a person later deletes %TEMP%\fsa-window-cases or %TEMP%\fsa-tests while %TEMP% is still compressed, the folder is recreated compressed and the refusal (and its remedy) comes round again. The message's other option, pointing TEMP and TMP elsewhere, is the lasting one.
Nothing new departed from the design in this round.

cases.evidence: HF-010: WindowCasesHelperTests.AllLeavesOutTheTimingCases is unchanged. It reads the real All branch and asserts T-005 and M-001 are absent, with T-004 and T-006 present.

HF-013: SmbLibraryPinTests now feeds both divergence shapes: a literal PackageReference version, and a csproj-level redefinition of the pin property (the builder recorded RED with a temporary 1.6.0 override in StallRig.csproj).

HF-027: the tests use real `compact /c` folders. TempTreeTests is now shaped like temp\fsa-tests\root, and the New-CaseFolder test like temp\fsa-window-cases\<guid>; both run the printed remedy and remake the folder. The New-CaseFolder test's post-remedy and left-behind assertions carry the m4 and m5 weaknesses, but on this machine it feeds the shape and passed.
